title: Alert rules, action groups and alert processing rules
learningObjective: Create metric, log search and activity log alert rules. Set up action groups. Use alert processing rules to send or silence notifications.
foundation: An alert rule watches a signal (a metric, a log query or an activity log event) and fires when its condition is met.
An action group says who to notify and what to run. An alert processing rule changes what happens to fired alerts, for example silencing them during maintenance.
engineer: An alert rule has four parts: scope, what to watch; condition, the signal, how to combine it, the comparison, a fixed or dynamic threshold, how far back to look and how often to check; actions, the action groups to call; details, severity 0 to 4 (0 is the most serious), name and auto-resolve.

Alert types: metric alerts, almost real time, and they resolve themselves when the problem goes away; log search alerts, a KQL query run on a schedule; activity log alerts, for example when a VM is deleted, or for Service Health and Resource Health events; smart detection; Prometheus alerts.
Action groups, who to tell: email, SMS, Azure app push notification, voice call, or email everyone with an Azure Resource Manager role.
Action groups, what to run: Automation runbook; Azure Functions; Event Hubs; ITSM tool; Logic Apps; webhook or secure webhook.
Action group tips: one action group can be used by many rules. SMS, voice and email have rate limits.

Alert processing rules: choose a scope (subscription, resource group or resource) and filters (severity, alert rule, resource type…). Then either add action groups, or silence notifications. You can give them a schedule, once or repeating.
Silenced still means fired: suppressed alerts still fire and still appear in the alerts list. Only the notifications are stopped.
Alert states: the condition is Fired or Resolved. Your response is New, Acknowledged or Closed.

example.title: Calling the right team
body: A metric alert fires when average CPU is above 80% for 5 minutes on any production VM. Its action group emails and texts the ops team, and calls a Logic App that opens a ticket.
An alert processing rule silences notifications every Sunday from 01:00 to 03:00, while patching runs.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with VMs to monitor or protect
permissions: Monitoring Contributor (alerts, diagnostic settings) or Backup Contributor (vaults, policies)
limits: See Azure Monitor / Azure Backup service limits
portal: Monitor > Alerts > Create > Alert rule: scope, condition, actions, details.
Monitor > Alerts > Action groups > Create: notifications and actions.
Monitor > Alerts > Alert processing rules > Create: scope, filters, suppress or apply action group, schedule.
configuration.cli:
az monitor action-group create -g rg-mon -n ag-ops --short-name ops --action email oncall oncall@contoso.com --action sms oncall 1 5555550100
az monitor metrics alert create -g rg-mon -n cpu-high --scopes $VM_ID --condition "avg Percentage CPU > 80" --window-size 5m --evaluation-frequency 1m --severity 2 --action ag-ops
az monitor alert-processing-rule create -g rg-mon -n suppress-patching --scopes /subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/rg-prod --rule-type RemoveAllActionGroups --schedule-recurrence-type Weekly --schedule-recurrence Sunday --schedule-recurrence-start-time 01:00:00 --schedule-recurrence-end-time 03:00:00
configuration.powershell:
$email = New-AzActionGroupEmailReceiverObject -Name oncall -EmailAddress oncall@contoso.com
New-AzActionGroup -ResourceGroupName rg-mon -Name ag-ops -ShortName ops -Location global -EmailReceiver $email
$c = New-AzMetricAlertRuleV2Criteria -MetricName 'Percentage CPU' -TimeAggregation Average -Operator GreaterThan -Threshold 80
Add-AzMetricAlertRuleV2 -Name cpu-high -ResourceGroupName rg-mon -TargetResourceId $vmId -Condition $c -WindowSize 00:05:00 -Frequency 00:01:00 -Severity 2 -ActionGroupId (Get-AzActionGroup -ResourceGroupName rg-mon -Name ag-ops).Id

lab.objective: Tune an alert so it fires on the spike, notifies the team and stays quiet during maintenance.
steps: Run the default (Average over 1 hour) and see the alert missed.

validation.text: Alert fired and notified the team
Saw an alert miss the spike
Saw an alert with no action group

failureScenarios: Expecting suppression to stop the alert itself
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.cause: The window or the Average smooths out the spikes, or the scope is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a shorter window or Maximum, and check the scope.

troubleshooting.symptom: The alert fires, but nobody is told.
troubleshooting.cause: No action group, or an alert processing rule silences it.
troubleshooting.fix: Add an action group, and check the processing rules.

troubleshooting.cause: Thresholds are too noisy, or rate limits kick in.
troubleshooting.fix: Use dynamic thresholds, and route by severity.

comparisons.difference: A CloudWatch alarm is like an alert rule. An SNS topic is like an action group.
Activity log alerts for Azure problems that affect your subscriptions.

misconceptions.reality: No. They add action groups or silence notifications. Alerts still fire.

misconceptions.myth: Each alert rule needs its own action group.
misconceptions.reality: No. Many rules can share one action group.

architectureDecisions: Use severities the same way everywhere: then route by severity with processing rules.
Noisy metrics: use dynamic thresholds, which learn what's normal.
Keep alert rules in code: Bicep or ARM, one set per environment.

walkthrough.subtitle: Be told about problems before users notice, and silence alerts during planned work.

steps.label: Silence
steps.title: The site was down for two hours and nobody knew
body: Charts are only useful if someone is looking. Alerts look for you.

steps.label: Rule
steps.title: An alert rule has three parts
body: Scope (which resources), condition (signal + logic, such as Percentage CPU > 80 averaged over 5 minutes), and actions (an action group). Plus details: name and severity 0 (critical) to 4 (verbose).

steps.label: Signals
steps.title: What can trigger an alert
body: Metrics, log search queries (KQL), activity log events (for example someone deleted a resource), resource health and service health.
Metric alerts are stateful by default: they fire once and resolve when the condition clears.

steps.label: Action group
steps.title: Action groups say who and how
body: An action group is reusable: notifications (email, SMS, push, voice) and actions (webhook, Logic App, Azure Function, Automation runbook, ITSM, Event Hub). Many rules can share one group.

steps.label: Processing
steps.title: Alert processing rules change alerts at scale
body: Alert processing rules apply to fired alerts across a scope: suppress notifications during maintenance windows, or add an action group to all alerts in a subscription. The alerts still fire and are recorded.

callout.text: Suppressed alerts still appear in the portal; only their actions are paused.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Alerts
body: Rule → alert → action group, adjusted by processing rules.
recap: Signals: metric, log, activity log, health
Processing rules suppress or add actions at scale

handsOn.title: Get an email when someone deletes a storage account
handsOn.cost: Free. Activity log alerts and email notifications cost nothing.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.
A storage account in rg-az104-lab that you are happy to delete.

steps.do: Search 'Monitor' > Alerts > Action groups > + Create. Group rg-az104-lab, name ag-lab, display name aglab. Notifications: Email, your address. Review + create > Create.
steps.see: A confirmation email saying you were added to ag-lab.

steps.do: Monitor > Alerts > + Create > Alert rule. Scope: rg-az104-lab.
Condition: signal 'Delete Storage Account (storageAccounts)' (activity log). Actions: select ag-lab. Details: name alert-delete-storage, severity 2. Create.
steps.see: The rule listed under Alert rules.

steps.do: Wait 2–5 minutes, then check your email and Monitor > Alerts.
steps.see: An email and a fired alert with the operation and who did it.

steps.do: Monitor > Alerts > Alert processing rules > + Create. Scope rg-az104-lab, rule type: Suppress notifications, schedule: always. Name apr-lab. Create.
Create another storage account and delete it.
steps.see: The alert fires again in the portal, but no email arrives: the processing rule suppressed it.

check: You received one alert email, and saw a later one suppressed.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
